title: Callable-output contract regression detector for post-quantization parity
creator: Aisha Gupta
description:
Goal: Build a deterministic test harness that detects regressions in callable/structured outputs after model artifacts are converted to low-precision profiles (FP8 and INT8). This ticket captures the engineering work to compare pre-quant and post-quant outputs against a contract (JSON schema + token-level constraints + required fields), record deltas, and surface actionable regressions to developers and CI.

Background: Prior calibration runs focused on token-level perplexity and end-to-end sampling quality. However, production infra has seen isolated cases where quantized variants produce syntactically invalid JSON or drop required keys in tool-calling payloads. These failures are high-severity for customers using programmatic tool chains. We need a targeted harness that: 1) runs across representative prompts and prompt families, 2) checks schema conformance and structural diffs, 3) tolerates acceptable semantic variance but flags contract breaches, and 4) plugs into CI and runtime monitoring for rolling quant-rollouts.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness can run batch comparisons between baseline FP32 (or prod float variant) and FP8/INT8 quantized model artifacts and produce a per-example verdict: PASS/FAIL and a compact delta report.
2) Define and enforce contract rules: JSON schema validation, required fields present, enum value restrictions, max-length constraints for string fields, and token provenance markers when applicable.
3) Contract pass rate for any quantized profile must be >= 99.9% on the canonical prompt set; failures produce a differential report that explains which field(s) regressed.
4) CI integration: quant-profile PRs that lower contract pass rate below threshold must block the merge and create an automatic issue with example traces.
5) Dashboard telemetry: per-profile pass rate, top failing prompts, and example payloads available in Console.
6) Alerts: if production rolling deploy sees >0.1% contract failures in live traffic for 30m, trigger oncall paging and automatic rollback if configured.
test_plan:
- Dataset: Curated corpus of 12k prompt families (API calls, tool invocation templates, form-fill tasks) with golden FP32 outputs and fallback tolerance annotations.
- Calibration workflow: Run calibration on INT8/FP8 candidate, then run the harness to compare 3 seeds of decoding (greedy/sample/temp=0.7) to capture nondeterminism.
- Validation checks: (a) JSON schema validation (ajv-compatible), (b) structural diffing (missing keys, type changes), (c) field-level token alignment where applicable (start/end indices), (d) business-rule smoke checks (e.g., currency fields numeric, ISO date format).
- Metrics: contract_pass_rate = passed_examples / total_examples; field_failure_rate; top-10 failing keys; average token-shift for numeric fields.
- Thresholds: pass_rate >= 99.9% for gating; for high-risk customers set provisional threshold 99.99%.
- Output artifacts: per-run report (compressed JSONL) plus a human-friendly HTML summary for triage.
- Regression capture: store 10 failing golden vs candidate pairs per profile and persist in S3 for later root cause analysis.
implementation_notes:
- Harness will be implemented in Rust for test runner speed (shared binary used by CI) with a Python shim to orchestrate calibration artifacts and Conductor job submission.
- Use existing calibration metadata schema produced by quant pipeline (scale factors, per-tensor stats) to tag runs.
- For schema validation use ajv (JS) for flexibility OR the Rust jsonschema crate where performance matters; keep equivalence across implementations.
- Add a lightweight token-level alignment module to map string field char offsets back to token indices to detect truncation/early-termination.
- The delta report format is flat JSONL records: example_id, profile, verdict, failing_fields[], sample_baseline, sample_quantized, concise_failure_reason. Keep each value as string-friendly fields for compatibility with existing logging pipelines.
- Instrumentation: emit metrics to telemetry (prometheus + honeycomb traces for example-level sampling).
- Provide a CLI: quant-contract-check --baseline <artifact> --candidate <artifact> --prompts <file> --out <report>.
- Integration with rollout: add a webhook that the rollout manager can query to decide automatic fallback when pass_rate drops below configured policy.
ci_integration:
- Add GH Actions job 'quant-contract-gate' that runs harness for changed artifacts in PRs that touch quantization/config. Use a sampled canonical subset for speed; full run runs in nightly.
- Gate rule: if sampled run < 99.5% pass then block and re-run with full canonical set; if full canonical < 99.9% fail PR.
- Upload compressed report to PR artifacts and post summary comment with top 3 failures and links to persisted failing traces.
- Nightly job to run all active profiles and emit dashboard metrics and anomalies as perf alerts.
- Unit and integration tests: mock calibration blobs, synthetic prompts to exercise edge cases (missing field, enum flip, number->string).
metrics_and_alerting:
- contract_pass_rate (per-profile, per-build) - alert when drop > 0.5% from baseline over 1h.
- failing_examples_count - alert when > 10 distinct failing examples in last 30m.
- top_failing_fields - used for routing to model team owners.
- time_to_triage (median) - measured from automated issue creation to first engineer comment; goal < 4h for P1.
- retention: store failing traces for 90 days.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- False positives: aggressive field-level checks may flag semantically equivalent but syntactically different responses; mitigate via fuzzy acceptance rules for specified prompt families.
- Cost vs coverage: full canonical runs are expensive; use two-tier sampling (fast subset in PRs, exhaustive nightly) to balance developer feedback velocity and coverage.
- Calibration masking: some calibration routines introduce small token shifts; decide whether to adjust thresholds per-model based on observed stable calibration delta.
- Runtime performance: additional token-level alignment adds CPU cost to the harness but is offline; do not run on hot paths.
- Rollout sensitivity: automated rollback is powerful but risks oscillation; require a confirmed anomaly window before automatic fallback for public tenants.
- Edge-case: hallucinated keys vs missing keys — missing required keys are high-severity and should always fail, hallucinated optional keys should be warned but not necessarily block gating.
